parameters.No symmetry: Generate zones independently, without a reflection constraint.
parameters.Face only symmetry: Place paired zones in corresponding regions of the connection graph, then let their positions evolve independently.
parameters.Embedding symmetry: Keep paired zone centers mirrored during placement. Zone shapes, walls and resources may differ.
parameters.Complete symmetry: Mirror the entire map, including zone shapes, walls, passages and resources. Diagonal reflection requires a square map.
parameters.Random magnet rotation: Rotate all magnet targets together by a seeded angle that keeps them inside the map. Relative distances and forces stay the same.
parameters.Magnet: Attract this zone toward its saved target during generation, independently of attraction to the map center.
parameters.Magnet force: Strength of attraction to the target, from 0.1 to 100. Default: 1. Higher values hold the zone closer; the minimum still attracts.
parameters.Magnet position: Target coordinates within the map frame: (0, 0) at the top left, (1, 1) at the bottom right. Moving zones or resizing the frame changes targets.
parameters.Template name: Display name in the editor and generator, separate from the filename.
parameters.Zone ID: Unique non-negative whole number. Changing it also updates this zone's connections and directed rules.
parameters.Radius: Relative zone size and spacing. Larger values give the zone more growth seeds, without guaranteeing its final area.
parameters.Susceptibility: Attraction to the map center. Positive values attract, negative values repel, and zero is neutral.
parameters.Boundary placement: Require an outer or inner position in the connection graph, or allow either. This does not guarantee contact with the final map edge.
parameters.Custom wall material: Override the default wall material, Cliff rock.
parameters.Wall material: Material used for walls between zones.
parameters.Octave count: Number of noise layers, from one to three. Removing a layer removes its weights from all zones.
parameters.Minimum radius: Smallest noise feature radius for this layer. Must be positive and no greater than the maximum.
parameters.Maximum radius: Largest noise feature radius for this layer. Larger radii produce broader resource patches.
parameters.Custom weight: Set this noise layer's contribution for the zone. When disabled, its weight is zero.
parameters.Weight: Contribution to the zone's resource noise. Higher values give this layer more influence; zero removes its contribution.
parameters.Material: Resource assigned to this noise interval and shown as a colored band in the zone square.
parameters.Start threshold: Lower bound of the resource's noise interval, from 0 to 1.
parameters.End threshold: Upper bound of the resource's noise interval, from its start to 1.
parameters.Limit map size: Restrict the map sizes available for this template in the Generator.
parameters.min: Inclusive lower bound. Aspect ratio is width divided by height.
parameters.max: Inclusive upper bound. The range must allow at least one supported map size.
parameters.Minimum passage width: Smallest opening through a zone border, in cells.
parameters.Maximum passage width: Largest opening through a zone border, in cells.
parameters.Minimum wall length: Shortest wall segment between passages, in cells.
parameters.Maximum wall length: Longest wall segment between passages, in cells. Zero allows continuous openings.
parameters.Resource blending: Mix resources across the border in both directions. Directed rules control each direction separately.
parameters.Blend distance: Blending reach across the border, in cells. Zero disables shared blending.
parameters.Preferred center distance: Set a target distance between zone centers during generation. Otherwise, spacing follows their radii.
parameters.Center distance: Target distance in map cells. Map bounds and other placement constraints may prevent an exact match.
parameters.Custom distance weight: Override the strength of the spacing preference. Default: 1.
parameters.Distance weight: Priority of this connection's spacing preference. Zero disables the preference while keeping the connection.
parameters.Enable directed rule: Apply resource influence in the displayed direction, independently of the reverse rule.
parameters.Intake distance: Reach of this rule's resource influence, in cells.
parameters.Guaranteed area: Cell budget for guaranteed resource influence near this border, separate from the zone's total area.
parameters.Bonus value: Additional resource influence from this rule. Higher values strengthen its contribution.

text.symmetry_warning: Symmetry could not be established. Details below. The template can still be edited and saved.
text.selection_mode:
Selection mode (V)
Select and move zones. Ctrl-click or box-select for multiple zones.
text.edge_mode:
Connection mode (E / hold Shift)
Connect two zones.
text.magnet_mode:
Magnet mode (M / hold Alt)
Click to toggle a magnet; drag to adjust force. Wheel resizes the map frame.
text.boundary_mode:
Boundary mode (B)
Click to cycle Any, Outer and Inner placement.
text.boundary_outer: Boundary: Outer - touches the outer face of the connection graph, without a fixed side or position.
text.boundary_inner: Boundary: Inner - enclosed by connections, away from the graph's outer face.
text.fit_magnet_frame: Fit the map frame around all zones. This changes magnet targets.
text.fit_graph: Fit all zones in view (F / Home)
text.dimensions: Width and height must be even, from 32 to 128. Aspect ratio is width / height.
text.resource_intervals: Intervals must cover 0 to 1 without gaps or overlaps.
text.invert_connection: Reverse the directed rules between these zones.
text.directed_rule_color: Matches this rule's arrow on the canvas. Rules with identical settings share a color.
text.map_adjust_other: Width and height adjust together to stay within this ratio.
text.map_adjusted: Size adjusted to fit this template.
text.topology_warning: A valid layout could not be found. Auto place is unavailable. The template can still be edited and saved.
text.auto_place: Arrange zones into a compact diagram with clear connections. Position magnets follow the new layout.
text.auto_place_disabled: Unavailable because of a connection or boundary placement issue. See the warning for details.

help.title: Template basics
paragraphs: Zones define relative size, attraction to the map center and resources. Resource intervals cover noise values from 0 to 1 and color the zone square from bottom to top. Noise octaves set patch sizes; each zone's weights set their contributions.

Connections define walls, passages and blending between zones. Directed rules control resource influence in each direction. Arrows point toward the receiving zone; matching colors indicate identical rule settings. Reverse connection swaps the directed rules.
Canvas positions describe the diagram. Position magnets use those positions as generation targets; connection spacing otherwise comes from radii or a preferred center distance.
Use for generation selects a snapshot of the template. Later edits do not update that snapshot. Drafts can be saved even when they are not ready for generation.

help.title: Symmetry modes
paragraphs: No symmetry places zones independently. Face only symmetry starts paired zones in corresponding regions of the connection graph, then lets their positions evolve independently. Embedding symmetry keeps paired centers mirrored throughout placement and relaxation, while shapes and resources may differ. Complete symmetry mirrors the final tiles as well.
Symmetry pairs zones and connections with matching generation settings. IDs and canvas coordinates do not determine pairs. Embedding and Complete symmetry also require compatible magnet targets.

The seed chooses orientation unless magnets guide it. Complete symmetry supports horizontal and vertical axes, plus both diagonals on square maps. Random magnet rotation keeps the chosen axis compatible with the grid.
The warning explains incompatible settings or a missing reflection. A search limit means the result is inconclusive. Crossed lines in the diagram alone do not rule out symmetry.

help.title: Canvas
paragraphs: Double-click empty space to add a zone, or a zone or connection to edit it. Drag a zone to move the selection. Drag empty space to box-select; Ctrl-click adds or removes individual zones. Hold Ctrl while dragging to snap to the grid.

V selects zones, E connects them, M adjusts magnets, and B sets boundary placement. Hold Shift for temporary Connection mode or Alt for Magnet mode. Ctrl+B cycles boundary placement for the selection; mixed selections become Outer.
Wheel zooms at the pointer. Middle or right drag pans. In Magnet mode, wheel resizes the map frame and Ctrl+wheel zooms. F or Home fits the diagram in view.
Ctrl+A selects all; Enter edits the selection; Delete removes it; Escape clears it or cancels a pending connection. Auto place arranges the diagram without overlaps or crossings and can be undone.

help.title: Boundary placement
paragraphs: Any allows either position. Outer requires contact with the connection graph's outer face. Inner requires enclosure by connections. These constraints take priority over magnets, but do not guarantee contact with the final map's edge tiles.

Outer zones have cyan badges and dashed links to the frame; the links do not fix a side or position. Inner zones have purple inset badges. Boundary placement is also available in Zone settings and the context menu.
Inner placement needs enclosing connection cycles. Incompatible boundary rules appear in the warning, even when the graph itself is planar.

help.title: Position magnets
paragraphs: Position magnets attract zones toward targets during generation. Stronger force holds a zone closer, subject to map bounds and connection constraints. Susceptibility controls a separate attraction to the map center.

In Magnet mode, click a zone to toggle its magnet. Drag outward to increase force or toward the center to reduce it. The glow indicates strength. The minimum force still attracts; toggling the magnet disables it.

Targets come from zone positions within the square map frame. The frame fits all zones, including those without magnets. Resizing it changes targets; panning and zooming do not. Fit frame resets its padding.

Random magnet rotation turns the target arrangement around the map center without changing forces or relative distances. The seed chooses an angle where all targets fit. Targets near corners allow fewer angles.

help.title: Copying and history
paragraphs: Copy data uses the active connection or last clicked zone. Paste data applies settings to the selected connection or all selected zones, preserving their IDs, positions and connections.
Connection data includes both directed rules, matched by endpoint order. A disabled source direction clears the matching destination rule. Zone and connection data are separate clipboard types.

Undo and redo cover document edits, including group moves and applied settings. Within a settings dialog they also cover individual edits before Apply. Selection and camera movement do not enter history.

help.title: Settings
paragraphs: Settings take effect on Apply; Enter also applies them. Escape or Cancel closes the dialog, with confirmation for unapplied changes. Undo and redo remain available while editing.
